mcp.ambiguous_topic: {topic!r} matches several topics: {matches}; pass the exact title and niche
mcp.cmd_help: run the MCP server on stdio (tools: trends_for_niche, upcoming, gsc_gaps, explain_topic)
mcp.instructions: nicheclock lists what is rising, what is dated ahead and when to publish. This server runs on your machine and reads the data of your last `nicheclock run`; it never fetches.
mcp.int_range: {what} must be an integer between {lo} and {hi}
mcp.judge_prompt: Judge this topic for the site above. Score 0-100 how well it fits the niche and the site's audience (90+ squarely on-niche and worth writing now; 60-89 related with a good angle; 30-59 tangential; below 30 off-niche, spam or ephemeral), give one sentence of reasoning that cites the evidence, and say whether an article should be published and by when. Use only the evidence returned here; do not invent facts about the topic.
mcp.no_data: no data yet for project {project!r}: run `nicheclock run` first
mcp.no_topic: no topic matching {topic!r} in the last 30 days; closest titles: {titles}
mcp.region_invalid: region must be 'global' or a two-letter country code such as US, GB or VN, got {region!r}
mcp.tool.explain: Evidence for one topic (title or key from trends_for_niche): its signals with sources and links, the niche definition, the site profile and top search queries, plus a judging prompt. Nothing is scored server-side: judge the niche fit with your own model.
mcp.tool.gaps: Search Console content gaps for a project: queries with real impressions where the site ranks beyond position 20 or has no matching page. Sorted by opportunity score.
mcp.tool.trends: Trending topics for one niche of a project over the last `days` days (default 7), best score first. Each has title, score, why (the evidence), url, sources and region (a country code, 'multi' or 'global') with region_precision. Pass `region` (e.g. US) to get that country's topics plus the global ones.
mcp.tool.upcoming: Dated upcoming events for a project in the next `days` days (default 30), soonest first, with publish_by (the date to publish by so the page is indexed in time), days_until and region. Pass `region` (e.g. US) to get that country's events plus the global ones.
mcp.topic_required: topic must be a title or key from trends_for_niche
mcp.unknown_niche: unknown niche {niche!r} in project {project!r}; known niches: {niches}
mcp.withheld_note: The terms of this item's source forbid AI/ML use, so its evidence is withheld: do not judge it with a model.
